question: Count-model cis-QTL permutations refit the covariate-only null for every permutation (the response and log-library offset shuffled together) and score it against the gene's cis genotypes. The design is the same for every permutation of a gene. Can the permuted nulls be fitted, and the permutations scored, in batches, and does it pay?

agreement_poisson.note: The Beta calibration brackets the reference noncentrality on [0, 100]. For a Poisson null of overdispersed counts the permutation maxima are inflated, the noncentrality reaches the cap, and the Beta MLE becomes ill-posed (n of 1e7 to 1e14), so rounding-level changes in the maxima move it. All 141 Poisson genes at the cap, and all 35 with n above 1e7, are listed by the run tables; genes below the cap agreed to 3.3e-13 relative in Beta p. The listed genes are every gene whose Beta p moved by more than 1e-6 relative or whose status changed. Statistics, lead variants, permutation counts and empirical p-values are identical for every gene.

null_fit_agreement.note: A diagnostic build refitted every lockstep fit with fit() (chr22, 100 permutations per gene, 58,000 fits per family): largest relative differences of coefficients (to 1 + |b|), theta and working weights. No lockstep fit fell back on chr22.

alternatives.name: 1.6.0-dev.1: one fit() and one cross_products call per permutation
block scores (eight permutations per blocked product, genotypes packed once per gene), separate fits
alternatives.result: bit for bit the dev.1 tables; 1.24x on chr22 NB

alternatives.name: block scores plus lockstep fits (chosen default)
alternatives.result: NB: fits within 1e-12 of fit(), Beta p within 8e-11, every other output identical; 1.35x on chr22 NB. Poisson: fits within 1.4e-13 of fit() and Beta p within 3.3e-13 wherever the reference noncentrality is below its cap of 100; on ill-posed Beta fits (noncentrality at the cap, n above 1e7) rounding moved eight Beta p-values by 2.3e-5 to 9.5% and failed one Beta fit (eGenes 30 to 29); 1.30x on chr22 Poisson

alternatives.name: single-precision score products (as the Gaussian path)
alternatives.result: not measured: roughly half the product time, but Beta p-values would move at the 1e-6 level, beyond rounding

alternatives.name: genotype-class sums (dosages 0/1/2: sums of weighted rows instead of products)
alternatives.result: not measured: about half the operations (54% of chr22 dosages are zero), but a different summation, so rounding beyond the current fits

alternatives.name: warm starts for permuted nulls
alternatives.result: not measured: they change the iterates beyond rounding; lockstep already cut the refits by about a third and they are no longer the bottleneck

choice: Default permutation_fits lockstep with block scoring; permutation_fits separate keeps per-permutation fit() calls and reproduces 1.6.0-dev.1 bit for bit. Open for the coordinator: on chr22 Poisson the lockstep fits agree to rounding, but their rounding moves nine ill-posed Beta fits beyond it, so the Poisson default may instead be separate.
reasons: The score products were 81% of the time; blocking them (same sums in the same order, better tiles, genotypes packed once) is bit-identical and gives most of the gain.

Lockstep fits replicate fit()'s algorithm; on chr22 NB they agree with it to 1e-12 and change no status, lead variant, statistic, empirical p-value or eGene, and they make the run about 9% faster than separate fits.
On chr22 Poisson the fits agree as closely, but 35 genes have ill-posed Beta fits (noncentrality at its cap of 100, n above 1e7) that rounding can move; nine of them moved beyond 1e-6.
Gaussian QTL is unchanged byte for byte.
